transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I'm here for my five-month diabetes and blood pressure check, that's the main reason I came. I have been having some pain in my right shoulder as well.
When did the pain in your right shoulder first start?
I'm not sure exactly when it started, but there was no injury or anything like that before it began. It just came on by itself.
Do you have any allergies to medicines?
No, I'm not aware of any allergies to medicines.
On a scale from 0 to 10, where 0 means no pain and 10 means the worst pain you can imagine, how bad is the pain in your right shoulder?
I can't really put a number on it, I'm afraid. It's not there all the time — certain movements of the shoulder are what make it hurt.
Could you tell me what medicines you take regularly these days, and how often you take them?
I take tablets for my diabetes and for my blood pressure, but I'm afraid I can't remember the names of them or the doses.
Besides the pain when you move it, has your shoulder been causing you any other trouble?
No, nothing else that I've noticed. There's no weakness, and no numbness or tingling in the arm.
Is there anything that's been on your mind about your health that you'd like to talk about today?
Not really — I came for my five-month diabetes and blood pressure check, and that's my main concern. The shoulder pain is the only other thing I've been noticing.
Could you tell me what the pain in your shoulder feels like when you notice it?
I can't describe it very well, I'm afraid. It's just a pain that comes on when I move my shoulder a certain way.
Is there anything else you'd like to add about your medicines?
No, there's nothing else — I'm afraid I just don't remember the names or the doses of my tablets.
How has your sleep been lately?
My sleep has been fine, thank you. I haven't had any trouble with it.
Have you ever had any operations?
I had a benign breast biopsy back in June 2004 — I was told it wasn't anything to worry about. I haven't had any operations besides that.
Is there anything that seems to make your shoulder pain better or worse?
Moving my shoulder in certain ways makes it worse, but I haven't noticed anything in particular that makes it better.
Have you had any health problems in the past that a doctor diagnosed or treated, such as a long-term condition or a one-off illness — or are you not sure?
Yes, I have type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure — those are the two long-term conditions I'm being seen for. The breast biopsy in 2004 was the other thing, and that turned out to be benign.
Is there anything else about your past health that you'd like to add?
Well, after that breast biopsy in 2004, I was told to come back for a repeat mammogram in six months, and I never did go for it. That's about all I can think of.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
